title: Chaos Theory × Neuroscience × Linguistics
content_html:
Chaos Theory × Neuroscience × Linguistics

Core Concepts

Nonlinear Feedback

Outputs feed back into inputs in ways that are not proportional; behavior depends on current state.

xt+1 = r xt(1-xt)

Model: logistic map; exhibits stability → cycles → chaos as r increases.

Attractors

Long-term patterns of behavior that trajectories approach (fixed, cyclic, strange).

Strange attractors: structured yet non-repeating patterns.

Sensitive Dependence

Small changes in initial conditions lead to divergent outcomes (“butterfly effect”).

Deterministic yet hard to predict long-term.

Alignment Map

Mathematics

  • Nonlinear iterated maps and differential equations
  • Attractors & basins; bifurcations
  • Fractals; power laws

Neuroscience (Memory & Perception)

  • Attractor networks (Hopfield); hippocampal replay
  • Prediction-error cycles; E/I balance
  • Reconsolidation reshapes basins of attraction

Linguistics (Use, Change, Structure)

  • Semantic drift; lexical innovation waves
  • Conversation dynamics; repair; turn-taking
  • Recursive syntax (self-similar structure)

One-to-One Correspondences

Sensitivity ↔ Cue-Driven Recall ↔ Pragmatic Shifts

Small cues (smell, word fragment) push neural state toward different memories; small contextual changes flip discourse interpretation.

Attractors ↔ Engrams/Schemata ↔ Constructions

Stable neural patterns underlie familiar stories; linguistic constructions serve as attractors for phrasing and meaning.

Bifurcation ↔ Learning Phase Shift ↔ Grammaticalization

Parameter changes (neuromodulators, exposure) cause phase transitions in behavior; forms grammaticalize in jumps.

Implications for the “Membrane”

Reconstructive memory = trajectory through an attractor landscape; each recall can deepen or reshape basins.

Feedback loops = nonlinear gains that can stabilize (negative) or amplify (positive) forms; chaos sits at the edge between them.

Language change = diffusion near bifurcation points; memes/metaphors become new attractors via social feedback.
